channel.description: Personally scored news, world affairs, opinion/analysis & foreign affairs, business & finance, and San Diego/local articles curated by news-filter

item.title: National Savings and Investments publishes latest interest rates for bonds and ISAs
item.description:
Source: FT News Feed Original headline: Latest National Savings & Investments rates
National Savings & Investments has released current interest rates for its various savings and investment products. Guaranteed Growth and Guaranteed Income Bonds (Issue 75) offer a 5.17% AER, with interest paid either yearly or monthly, subject to a minimum deposit of £500 and a maximum of £1m. Other bond issues offer lower rates, such as Issue 83 at 5.10% AER and Issue 81 at 5.07% AER. Green Savings Bonds (Issue 10) provide a 4.73% AER for deposits between £100 and £100,000. For liquid savings, the Direct Saver account offers a 3.75% AER, while the Investment Account provides 2.05% AER. Tax-free options include a Direct ISA at 3.80% AER with a maximum deposit of £20,000, and a Junior ISA at 3.70% AER for those able to reach age 18, with a maximum deposit of £9,000. All rates are shown as AER variable unless otherwise stated.

item.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal to reduce tariffs and secure raw materials
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
The European Union and Indonesia have signed a trade agreement that will gradually remove tariffs on more than 98% of product categories over 15 years. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the deal one of the bloc's "most ambitious deals" in the region, linking markets of 730 million people. For the EU, the agreement aims to secure access to critical raw materials like nickel, which is essential for electric vehicle batteries, while reducing strategic dependencies on China. Economist Yose Rizal Damuri estimates Indonesian exports could increase by around 60%, potentially benefiting textile, footwear, and furniture sectors. However, Damuri warned that Indonesia must improve its domestic business climate and production capacity to ensure actual export growth. Other challenges include Indonesia's need to meet European environmental and labor standards, such as the EU Deforestation Regulation. Analyst Eline Blot noted that while increased production could lead to pollution and ecosystem degradation, the priority should be providing smallholders with technical support to meet these regulations rather than weakening the requirements.

item.title: Nine injured after explosion and fire at Bangkok oil refinery
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
An explosion at the Phra Khanong oil refinery in eastern Bangkok injured nine people, leaving three in critical condition. The blast, which occurred around 14:45 (07:45 GMT), caused a fire at the Bangchak Corporation facility that was brought under control within 30 minutes. Black smoke was visible across the city skyline, prompting local officials to urge residents to avoid the area. Energy minister Akanat Promphan stated the impact appeared limited because the fire started in a distillation tower located approximately 100m (330ft) from oil storage. However, because the refinery is located in a residential area, the government has suspended production until operations can safely resume. Bangchak Corporation confirmed that production at the site, which has a capacity of up to 120,000 barrels of oil a day, has been shut down. Air quality monitoring in the immediate vicinity currently shows normal ranges. This incident follows a previous explosion at the Bangkok refinery in July 2012 that caused a fire but no injuries.

item.title: Police rescue 164 foreigners from cyberfraud and trafficking network near Delhi
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: India busts cyberfraud and trafficking network rescuing 164 foreigners
Police in India uncovered an international cyberfraud and human trafficking operation on the outskirts of Delhi, rescuing 92 Indonesian and 72 Malaysian nationals. Victims were allegedly lured to Noida with promises of lucrative IT jobs, but police say they were forced into cybercrime, including posing as women online to lure victims into fake investment platforms. One Malaysian national has been arrested, and authorities confiscated nearly 550 computers and mobile phones. The scheme was exposed after a Malaysian worker escaped and revealed the operation. This incident follows a surge in digital fraud; India's National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal recorded 2.8 million complaints in 2025, with losses totaling approximately 22,495 crore rupees. The federal government notes that most cases involve fake investment and trading scams where fraudsters promise high returns through social media or messaging. This investigation follows other recent raids in Lucknow and Pitampura, including a July operation in Lucknow where police arrested 119 people for targeting US citizens.

item.title: One dead after diesel tanker capsizes off the coast of Ibiza
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle
A Malta-flagged diesel tanker, the Med Emre, capsized off the coast of Ibiza, resulting in the death of one crew member. All 17 crew members were rescued, though seven were hospitalized, including at Ibiza's Can Misses Hospital and facilities in Valencia. The vessel was traveling from Algeciras to Barcelona when it reported a leak and a 90-degree lean. While initial reports suggested the ship sank to the seabed, regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz clarified the tanker remains partially submerged and drifting upside down. Maritime security expert Emilio Rodriguez Diaz noted the vessel's double-hull design acts as a buffer to prevent cargo release. Although maritime captain Elena Delgado reported a small slick had formed and then disappeared, authorities are monitoring the area for environmental damage to sensitive local biodiversity. The Transport Ministry reported that the rescue vessel Guardamar Talia saw no wreckage or signs of pollution as of Thursday morning. Spain's merchant marine authority has activated a level 2 national maritime pollution contingency plan.

item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 12,000 cases amid armed conflict
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has exceeded 12,000 confirmed cases, making it the fastest-growing outbreak in history. Congo's Ministry of Health reports that nearly half of the 12,021 confirmed cases have died. This outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, has no approved vaccine or treatment. It is currently on track to surpass the death toll of the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016. Containment efforts face significant disruption due to armed conflict between the army and Convention pour la révolution populaire rebels. Fighting in the mining town of Iga-Barrière has displaced people toward Bunia, a major response hub. World Health Organization Ebola incident manager Dr. Catherine Smallwood said fighting earlier this week prevented teams from reaching certain communities and left some treatment centers understaffed. On Tuesday, a dozen people, including two WHO personnel and Congolese health officials, were evacuated to Bunia after being trapped for three days in an Akwe hospital due to intense crossfire.

item.title: Chinese shares rise after State Council signals support for capital markets
item.description:
Source: FT World Original headline: Chinese shares soar after Beijing signals more support
Chinese stocks rose sharply on Friday following a rare expression of support from the State Council. The cabinet, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, stated that capital markets remain "crucial to overall economic development." The meeting readout called for increased share buybacks and dividend payouts from listed companies, while urging the "national team" of state-backed funds to step up its role in stabilizing the market. Following the announcement, the CSI 300 index closed up about 4 per cent, and the tech-focused Star 50 index advanced more than 15 per cent. This follows months of weakness, with the CSI 300 down more than 20 per cent from its June peak. Lotus Asset Management chief investment officer Hao Hong called the mention of a market stabilization fund "huge," suggesting the move could lead to a real bounce. Everbright Securities International strategist Kenny Ng said the tone signals to investors that policy reserves remain ready to be used. Other Asian markets also rose, including South Korea’s Kospi, which gained 4.3 per cent.

item.title: Hong Kong proposes tax breaks for sovereign wealth and pension funds
item.description:
Source: FT World Original headline: Hong Kong seeks to lure sovereign wealth funds with tax breaks
Hong Kong plans to introduce tax breaks for sovereign wealth and pension funds to compete with low-tax jurisdictions like Singapore and the Middle East. Under a proposed bill currently before the Legislative Council, a wider variety of funds would have investment gains exempt from corporation tax. Additionally, individual fund managers, including those managing sovereign and pension money, would be exempt from tax on performance-linked payouts. This move follows a period where some global investors scaled back operations due to a Chinese dealmaking drought and worsening US-China relations, such as Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan's plan to close its Hong Kong office. KPMG partner Darren Bowdern says sophisticated sovereign investors may prefer setting up their own structures to benefit from expanded carried interest tax concessions. If passed, the bill could apply retroactively to the 2025-26 tax year, allowing for tax refunds. The government aims to pass the bill before the end of the year to attract more funds, family offices, and global capital to the territory.

item.title: Police investigate after woman's body washes ashore in Newport Beach
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Woman's body washes ashore in Newport Beach; police investigate
Newport Beach police and the Orange County Coroner Division are investigating after an adult female body washed ashore near 34th Street on Thursday. Lifeguards discovered the body near the beach around 12:45 p.m. and alerted authorities. Lt. Court Depweg of the Newport Beach Police Department stated that the identity and circumstances of the deceased are currently under investigation. While specific details regarding the cause of death remain unavailable, the discovery occurs as coastal Southern California communities face hazardous beach conditions. Officials have warned of king tides, high surf, large waves, rip currents, and sneaker waves that have caused water to crash over seawalls and into homes.

item.title: Data centre developers target northern England industrial sites as London reaches saturation
item.description:
Source: FT World Original headline: English data centres head north
Data centre developers are moving toward northern England as land and power supplies near a saturation point in London. Developers are targeting former industrial sites, such as power stations and manufacturing plants, because these locations offer ready energy connections. Tom McWilliams of JLL notes that "power is the new planning," as these sites allow for the redeployment of energy previously used by heavy industry. Proposed large-scale projects include sites at Drax power station, Skelton Grange, and Fiddlers Ferry. Innova plans a 286MW campus near Dunham Massey in Cheshire, a proposal facing local opposition and a 5,000-signature petition. While Drax Group director Richard Gwilliam argues repurposing these sites could "reindustrialise" the north, local politicians like Richard Burgon and Esther McVey have raised concerns regarding environmental impacts. Currently, only Greater Manchester has published a formal data centre strategy, while other regional mayors in the north and Midlands are still developing plans to manage the fast-moving sector.

item.title: Bank of England governor warns AI breakthroughs could threaten financial data encryption
item.description:
Source: FT World Original headline: FirstFT: BoE’s Bailey warns of AI threat to encrypted financial data
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that recent AI-driven breakthroughs in mathematics could threaten the encryption used to safeguard financial data. In the bank's financial stability report, the BoE advised financial groups to prioritize updating cryptographic codes to protect against compromises from AI or quantum computing. Bailey noted that AI developers are currently on the "exponential part of the development curve" and expressed support for their caution regarding the release of increasingly powerful models. Meanwhile, US tech stocks face their worst monthly decline in nearly four years as market volatility increases. In Italy, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni criticized Ukraine for sinking a Russian warship at a Libyan naval base, stating, "The war must not, cannot spread to the Mediterranean." Additionally, legal texts reveal the UK will pay a new participation fee to the EU to remove certain food and drink export border checks and re-link carbon markets.

item.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from Lubero town amid diplomatic tensions with DR Congo
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row
Uganda will withdraw its troops from Lubero, in North Kivu province, within two weeks, handing security back to Congolese forces. The Ugandan army announced the move Friday following nearly two years of military operations in the town. The withdrawal follows a diplomatic row after Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of President Yoweri Museveni, appeared to endorse a rebel takeover of the mineral-rich Walikale territory. The Congolese foreign ministry called his remarks particularly serious, prompting Kinshasa to summon Uganda's top diplomat. The Uganda People's Defence Forces were originally deployed to Lubero to pursue fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), an Islamic State-affiliated group. While the planned withdrawal applies only to Lubero, spokesperson Col Chris Magezi said the joint military campaign, known as Operation Shujaa, will continue elsewhere in DR Congo. Acled analyst John Ngono noted that while Operation Shujaa may have improved security in Uganda, the ADF remains a deadly threat in DR Congo, killing an average of four civilians a day and expanding into new areas.

item.title: Opposition leaders in several African nations face legal and security-related restrictions
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure
Opposition leaders across Cameroon, Tanzania, Mozambique, Nigeria, and Zambia accuse authorities of using legal restrictions and security provisions to limit political freedoms. In Cameroon, Ndah Grimbald of the Social Democratic Front notes that the non-authorization of public rallies and lack of attention to private members' bills hinder opposition activity. In Tanzania, opposition leader Tundu Lissu was sentenced to four years in prison for incitement, a verdict he called "political persecution" intended to disrupt the 2025 general election. Tanzanian spokesperson Gerson Msigwa dismissed claims of repression as "unfounded and misleading." In Mozambique, Venancio Mondlane faces charges including incitement to terrorism following disputed 2024 election protests, though he denies encouraging violence. In Nigeria, police arrested men wearing "Tinubu Must Go!" shirts, citing suspected drugs and public disturbance rather than political views. In Zambia, opposition leader Brian Mundubile criticized the closure of courts during election petition filings, while former lawmaker Mutotwe Kafwaya was killed during a security operation at Mundubile's residence. Constitutional lawyer Linda Kasonde warned that democracy in Zambia is "on trial."

item.title: EU leaders fail to agree on long-term budget or Ukraine aid
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, FT World Original headline: EU leaders fail to reach agreement on long-term budget or Ukraine aid at Brussels summit
European Union leaders failed to reach a consensus on a proposed 2028-2034 budget of €1.582 trillion during a 12-hour summit in Brussels on Thursday. Negotiations are deferred until a December 17 and 18 summit. Disagreements persist over spending, with France and Italy advocating for higher spending for farming and regional development, while Germany seeks financial restraint. President Emmanuel Macron warned he would veto any deal cutting farmer subsidies or maintaining existing rebates for net-contributors like Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Denmark, and Austria. Additionally, Irish Premier Micheál Martin rejected a proposal to tax digital services to raise €35 billion. Regarding a proposed €45 billion loan for Ukraine, split into €20 billion for civil services and €25 billion for arms, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, and Hungary have objected, though 24 out of 27 members support it. Macron warned that upcoming French presidential elections in April could prevent a budget relaunch after this year. Meanwhile, the summit named economist Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next President of the European Central Bank, succeeding Christine Lagarde in February 2027.
item.source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, FT World

item.title: Guinea-Bissau military leaders postpone return to civilian rule until 2028
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Guinea-Bissau's military leaders delay return to civilian rule until 2028
Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have postponed presidential and parliamentary elections by two years, delaying the return to civilian rule. Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam announced via decree that the polls, originally scheduled for 6 December, will now be held on 26 November 2028. The presidency stated that an assessment found insufficient technical, material, and financial conditions to hold the vote as planned. This delay aims to ensure future elections are credible, transparent, and inclusive. Gen N'Tam assumed office a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025. That coup occurred three days after general elections and before provisional results could be announced, a period during which both Embaló and challenger Fernando Dias claimed victory. Embaló, currently in exile in Morocco, remains barred from returning to the country despite interest in contesting future votes. While the presidency reiterated a commitment to holding the nation's first local government elections, no date has been set for that vote.

item.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday due to storm safety concerns
item.description:
Source: ABC News: Top Stories Original headline: Bands drum up support so the show goes on for postponed Macy's Thanksgiving parade
New York City officials, the NYPD, and Macy's announced Wednesday that the 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday due to safety concerns caused by a massive storm. The rescheduled parade is now set to begin at 8:30 a.m. ET. While some groups like Concord Community High School's Marching Minutemen will participate because they planned to be in New York through the weekend, others face significant logistical hurdles. The Pride of Pearland High School Band and Color Guard from Texas successfully raised enough funds in under 24 hours to cover extra hotel and transportation costs for their group of over 500. Director Ryan Demkovich noted that community donations and even cash from people on the street in New York helped ensure the group could stay. Conversely, the University of Alabama's Million Dollar Band decided to return to Tuscaloosa to perform in the Iron Bowl instead of participating in the rescheduled event.

item.title: Black and tan coonhound Rocker wins best in show at National Dog Show
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Culture Original headline: Black and tan coonhound Rocker is top dog at the 2026 National Dog Show
Black and tan coonhound Rocker won best in show at the 2026 National Dog Show, held Nov. 14 and 15 at the Greater Philadelphia Expo Center. Rocker, owned by Traci Mitchell of Bedford, Iowa, previously won first place in the hound group before defeating six other group winners. Best in show judge Lorraine Bisso praised Rocker's masculine head, physical agility, and breed-correct structure, noting his way of being a hunting hound. Handler Mandy Clevenger, who has worked with Rocker since he was a pup, said the win was unexpected but that Rocker loves the crowd. This victory marks Rocker's 15th best in show title. Other group victors included Kissy, a lhasa apso; Biggie Smalls, a Newfoundland; and Rambo, a Norfolk terrier. The event was broadcast on NBC and streamed on Peacock, hosted by John O'Hurley, Mary Carillo, and David Frei. Rocker is expected to compete at the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show in New York City early next year.

item.title: Robotics and physical AI companies raise $97.3 billion in record funding year
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: From Waymo to Jeff Bezos' Prometheus, meet the biggest fundraisers in robotics and physical AI
Robotics and physical AI companies have raised $97.3 billion across more than 1,200 deals, more than doubling the $47.4 billion raised in 2025. F-Prime partner Sanjay Aggarwal attributes the surge to growth in autonomous vehicles, defense, domestic manufacturing, and high-profile founders. Waymo secured the year's largest round, a $16 billion Series D, valuing the company at $126 billion. Jeff Bezos and Vik Bajaj's Prometheus raised a $12 billion Series B to build an "artificial general engineer." In the defense sector, Anduril raised $5 billion, while Shield AI announced plans for a $2 billion package, including a $1 billion Series H. Other significant raisers include Zipline, which raised $1.5 billion, and Helsing, which secured $1.8 billion. Skild AI, developing machine-control models, raised $1.4 billion, and Neura Robotics, which is developing humanoids, also secured $1.4 billion. Crunchbase research lead Gené Teare notes that drones attract significant capital because the technology is more mature than other experimental robotics areas.

item.title: Two men killed in Temecula helicopter crash involving Robinson R22
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: SoCal Marine and father is one of two men killed in Temecula helicopter crash
Two men died Monday morning, Nov. 23, when a Robinson R22 helicopter slammed into a hillside near De Portola and Oak Mountain roads in Temecula. The Riverside County Sheriff’s Office identified the victims as 36-year-old Christopher Lamaku of Escondido and 26-year-old Steven Madrid of Yuma, Ariz. The aircraft had taken flight from French Valley Airport before the crash occurred around 9:30 a.m. Both men died at the scene. Lamaku, a former Marine, police officer, and pilot, was a reserve officer with the Escondido Police Department and a graduate of the Palomar College Police Academy. He is survived by a wife and a 4-year-old son. Friends described Madrid as a kind person who lived life on the edge. The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating the cause of the crash.

item.title: Two Italian technicians die in drone strike on Kuwaiti facility
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle Original headline: Two Italian technicians killed in drone strike on Kuwaiti facility
Two Italian technicians, aged 36 and 65, died during a drone strike on a vital facility in Kuwait. The men were employees of the Italian branch of Rheinmetall, performing maintenance on Skyguard air-defense system antennas. Kuwait's defense ministry reported that a Kuwaiti national and a Pakistani national were injured by falling shrapnel. While Kuwait's army characterized the strike as "heinous Iranian aggression," Iran denied responsibility. Iranian armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi stated no offensive operations had been conducted, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the incident "suspicious," warning it looked like a "precooked recipe for war." Investigations suggest the drone used was manufactured in Iran, noting that Iranian proxies frequently carry out regional attacks. This incident follows a period of heightened tension after Kuwait repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on a US-hosted airbase last week. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed sympathy for the victims' families, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for increased pressure on Iran to end attacks against its neighbors and partners in the Gulf.

item.title: Zelenskyy warns of imminent Russian attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure
item.description:
Source: ABC News: Top Stories Original headline: Zelenskyy warns of imminent major Russian attack on Ukraine’s power grid
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Thursday that Russia is preparing a massive new strike against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, targeting substations and power lines to deprive civilians of heat and light. Ukrainian crews are currently repairing damage in six regions following an overnight attack involving ballistic missiles and 113 drones that hit a hospital, businesses, and a gas station. Meanwhile, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner stated that Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons, though Kushner noted that peace talks face a deadlock over the fate of Ukrainian territory. Kushner, who is mediating talks with envoy Steve Witkoff, said Putin wants peace, but cautioned, "it’s always peace on what terms." Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Washington is "open to dialogue" and must address security threats on Russia's borders. As combat expands, including Ukrainian sea drone strikes on a Russian vessel in Libya, Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni urged that the war should not expand to the Mediterranean.

item.title: India calls special parliament sitting amid speculation over way certain bills
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: India's Modi government calls special sitting of parliament
The Indian government has called a special sitting of parliament, with the Lok Sabha scheduled to meet on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2. This reconvening follows an indefinite adjournment of the monsoon session in August. While official communications mention transacting "essential Government Business," speculation suggests the government may attempt to pass a Delimitation Bill to redraw constituency boundaries and a bill for a 33% women's quota in Parliament. The opposition Congress party, led by figures such as Jairam Ramesh, has criticized the move, calling it an "assault on the Constitution" and accusing the government of seeking a fraudulent two-thirds majority. Separately, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that a trade deal with the United States is "close to culmination," even as the US proposes tariffs on Indian imports. Meanwhile, India has presented a bid to the International Olympic Committee to host the 2036 Olympics in Ahmedabad, with IOA chief executive Raghuram Iyer expressing hope for advancing to the next stage.

item.title: Venezuela to repeal law barring opposition figures from public office
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
National Assembly Speaker Jorge Rodríguez announced that Venezuela will repeal the Simón Bolívar Law, which bars certain opposition figures from holding public office. The legislation, passed following the July 2024 election, permanently banned any individual who requested or supported foreign sanctions from political office and mandated the confiscation of their assets. While critics argue the law enables political persecution, Rodríguez stated that no politician had been subjected to its provisions and noted the law responded to a specific, temporary situation. The repeal is expected to be approved next week as part of a "route map towards democracy" being negotiated between interim president Delcy Rodríguez and opposition parties. These negotiations follow the seizure of former President Nicolás Maduro by the United States at the start of the year. Although the electoral authority declared Maduro the winner of the July election, the opposition maintains that Edmundo González won, citing evidence from voting tallies. Opposition leader María Corina Machado, who returned from exile in October, is expected to run for office if free and fair elections are held.
